subject: running code in version 0.6-11, not working in 0.6-12

messages.author: 20690f23c3a86c45
messages.subject: running code in version 0.6-11, not working in 0.6-12
parts:
Hi all,

I'm a recent user of nimble, I was working on a simple linear multivariate model on a machine that had the 0.6-11 version of nimble.
Everything was working fine, bu I have now moved on a machine that has the 0.6-12 version installed on and i get the following error during the compiling step:

'Error: Failed to create the shared library'


See below the model's code


model_nimble2 <- nimbleCode({

   ## Priors
  
  sigma~dunif(0,10)
  tau <- pow(sigma,-2)

  sigma_pred~dunif(0,100)
  tau_pred <- pow(sigma_pred,-2)
    
  beta0 ~ dnorm(0,0.01)
  beta0_pred ~ dnorm(0,0.01)
  
  for(k in 1:K){
    beta[k] ~ dnorm(0,0.01)
    beta_pred[k] ~ dnorm(0,0.01)
  }

  for (i in 1:n_reading){
    Dat[i,10]~ dnorm(mu[i], tau)
    mu[i] <-  beta0 + beta[1] * Dat[i,8] + 
      beta[2] * Dat[i,11] + beta[3] * Dat[i,12]
    
    ## Predict the True length based only on covariates available in "normal" conditions
       Dat_pred[i,8] ~ dnorm(mu_pred[i], tau_pred)
    mu_pred[i] <- beta0_pred + beta_pred[1] * Dat_pred[i,10] + beta_pred[2] * Dat_pred[i,11] + 
      beta_pred[3] * Dat_pred[i,12] 
 
  }
  ## END model
}

)

Constants are entered as follow (Dat is a data frame

nimble_data <- list(K=K,
                    n_fish=n_fish,
                    n_reading=n_reading , 
                    fish_r=fish_r,
                    Dat=Dat,
                    Dat_pred = Dat,
                    mu=rep(0,n_reading),
                    mu_pred=rep(0,n_reading)
)




Thanks in advance for any help/suggestion

G

Hi Guillaume, could you send us a full reproducible example (by
providing the values that are used in constructing nimble_data, and
showing how you create the model and do the compilation?
Feel free to share simulated data rather than the real data if you prefer.

Also please let us know the output of the compileNimble call when use
include "showCompilerOutput=TRUE" as an argument to the call.

chris
